memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded. He raised his staff in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water was changed into blood. The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad that the Egyptians could not drink its water. Blood was everywhere in Egypt." - Exodus 7:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again the text says it plainly: Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded. That phrase is becoming the quiet backbone of this book.

Everything that follows depends on that simple obedience. Moses did not have to make the water turn to blood. He only had to raise the staff. God did the rest.

That division of labour is worth remembering. Our part is usually small, ordinary and within reach — speak the word, make the visit, give the gift, tell the truth, raise the staff. God's part is the transformation, which we could never manufacture.

We often get this backwards. We attempt God's part and neglect our own. We agonise over outcomes we cannot control while leaving undone the simple act of obedience in front of us.

Notice too that this happened in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials. It was public. God was not hiding what He was doing.

Do your small part today. Leave the river to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What simple act of obedience is in front of me right now?
2. Am I anxious about an outcome that was never mine to produce?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to do my part faithfully and to trust You with everything beyond my reach. Amen.
